121. The pace of implementation of the government's 2014-16 reform program

could be slowed down by institutional capacity risks in the event of changes of key

personnel and lack of reform will. The phased approach through a series of DPCs is a

risk-mitigating factor. The actions supported under the proposed series of DPCs form the

second phase of the medium-term government financial sector reform program initiated in

2012. This multi-stage approach has helped to gradually generate and solidify consensus

on the broader reform program, and most prior actions for DPC2 reflect the extensive work

done to fulfill the prior actions for DPC1. Legislative risks posed by the need for

Parliament to focus on completing the new constitution in its first year of operation are

mitigated by limiting DPC2 legislative prior actions to submission to Parliament of two

key pieces of financial sector legislation (NRBAA and DCGFA) for which there is firm
